sentences.zh: 周處

translations.literal: Zhou Chu — biography heading.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Chu.

sentences.zh: 周處，字子隱，義興陽羨人也。

translations.literal: Zhou Chu, courtesy name Ziyin, was a native of Yangxian in Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Chu, courtesy Ziyin, came from Yangxian in Yixing commandery.

sentences.zh: 父魴，呉鄱陽太守。

translations.literal: His father Fang was Wu Administrator of Poyang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhou Fang had served Wu as prefect of Poyang.

sentences.zh: 處少孤，未弱冠，膂力絶人，好馳騁田獵，不修細行，縱情肆欲，州曲患之。

translations.literal: Chu was orphaned young; before the capping age his bodily strength cut off others; he loved galloping and hunting fields and wastes; he did not cultivate minor conduct; indulged emotion and unleashed desire—the district dreaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned before adulthood, he was immensely strong and devoted himself to hunting and carousing until the countryside feared him.

sentences.zh: 處自知爲人所惡，乃慨然有改勵之志，謂父老曰：「今時和歳豐，何苦而不樂耶？

translations.literal: Chu himself knew he was hated by men; thereupon indignant had the intent of reform and exertion; he said to village elders: "Times are harmonious and years abundant—why suffer and not rejoice?"
translations.idiomatic: Knowing people despised him, he resolved to mend his ways and asked the elders why anyone should be unhappy in such good harvests.

sentences.zh: 」父老歎曰：「三害未除，何樂之有！

translations.literal: " The elders sighed saying: "The three scourges not removed—what joy is there!"
translations.idiomatic: They answered that three scourges still plagued the land—there was little to celebrate.

sentences.zh: 」處曰：「何謂也？

translations.literal: " Chu said: "What is meant?"
translations.idiomatic: "What scourges?" he asked.

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「南山白額猛獸，長橋下蛟，並子爲三矣。

translations.literal: " They replied: "South Mountain's white-browed fierce beast; beneath Long Bridge the crocodilian dragon—and together with you there are three."
translations.idiomatic: They named the white tiger on South Mountain, the river dragon under Long Bridge, and Zhou Chu himself.

sentences.zh: 」處曰：「若此爲患，吾能除之。

translations.literal: " Chu said: "If these make calamity, I can remove them."
translations.idiomatic: "Then I will rid you of them," he vowed.

sentences.zh: 」父老曰：「子若除之，則一郡之大慶，非徒去害而已。

translations.literal: " The elders said: "If you remove them, then it is one commandery's great blessing—not merely removing harm."
translations.idiomatic: The elders replied that slaying the beasts would bless the whole commandery.

sentences.zh: 」處乃入山射殺猛獸，因投水搏蛟，蛟或沈或浮，行數十里，而處與之俱，經三日三夜，人謂死，皆相慶賀。

translations.literal: " Chu thereupon entered the mountains and shot dead the fierce beast; then threw himself in the water to grapple the dragon; the dragon sometimes sank or floated; traveled several tens of li while Chu together with it went; passing three days three nights; people said he was dead—all mutually rejoiced and congratulated.
translations.idiomatic: He shot the tiger, then fought the dragon midstream for tens of li over three days until watchers assumed both were dead and celebrated.

sentences.zh: 處果殺蛟而反，聞鄕里相慶，始知人患己之甚，乃入呉尋二陸。

translations.literal: Chu indeed killed the dragon and returned; hearing his village rejoicing together, first knew men dreaded him extremely; thereupon entered Wu seeking the two Lus.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned alive and heard the rejoicing, he grasped how hated he had been and went to Wu to study under the Lu brothers.

sentences.zh: 時機不在，見-{雲}-，具以情告，曰：「欲自修而年已蹉跎，恐將無及。

translations.literal: At the time Ji was not present; he saw Yun and fully reported the situation saying: "I wish to cultivate myself but years already slip away—fear it will be too late."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ji was away, so he poured out his heart to Lu Yun, fearing he had wasted his youth.

sentences.zh: 」-{雲}-曰：「古人貴朝聞夕改，君前途尚可，且患志之不立，何憂名之不彰！

translations.literal: " Yun said: "The ancients prized hearing at dawn and reforming at evening—your forward road still permits; moreover worry not that intent is not established—why fret that fame is not displayed!"
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yun assured him that moral awakening could come late—resolve mattered more than lost years.

sentences.zh: 」處遂勵志好學，有文思，志存義烈，言必忠信克己。

translations.literal: " Chu thereupon urged his intent and loved learning; had literary thought; intent lodged in righteous fierceness; speech always loyal and trustworthy, conquering self.
translations.idiomatic: Chu devoted himself to letters and upright conduct, speaking always with integrity.

sentences.zh: 期年，州府交辟。

translations.literal: After one full year province and prefecture mutually summoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year every province and prefecture sought him.

sentences.zh: 仕呉爲東觀左丞。

translations.literal: He served Wu as Left Assistant of the Eastern Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wu he became left aide at the Eastern Pavilion archive.

sentences.zh: 孫皓末，爲無難督。

translations.literal: At the end of Sun Hao he was Trouble-Free Corps commander.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao's last years made him commander of the Trouble-Free corps.

sentences.zh: 及呉平，王渾登建鄴宮釃酒，既酣，謂呉人曰：「諸君亡國之餘，得無戚乎？

translations.literal: When Wu was pacified, Wang Hun ascended Jianye palace and sprinkled wine; already drunk, he said to Wu men: "You gentlemen are remnants of a lost state—could there be no sorrow?"
translations.idiomatic: After Wu fell Wang Hun toasted the conquered Wu officials and taunted them about grief.

sentences.zh: 」處對曰：「漢末分崩，三國鼎立，魏滅-{於}-前，呉亡於-{後}-，亡國之戚，豈惟一人！

translations.literal: " Chu replied: "Late Han split and collapsed; three kingdoms stood like tripod vessels—Wei perished first; Wu perished afterward—the sorrow of a lost state—how could it be only one man!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Chu answered that Wei had fallen before Wu—many had known defeat, not they alone.

sentences.zh: 」渾有慚色。

translations.literal: " Hun had ashamed color.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hun flushed with embarrassment.

sentences.zh: 入洛，稍遷新平太守。

translations.literal: Entering Luoyang, gradually promoted Administrator of Xinping.
translations.idiomatic: In Luoyang he rose to prefect of Xinping.

sentences.zh: 撫和戎狄，叛羌歸附，雍土美之。

translations.literal: He soothed harmoniously Rong and Di; rebel Qiang returned and attached; Yong lands praised him.
translations.idiomatic: He pacified tribes until rebel Qiang submitted and Yongzhou admired him.

sentences.zh: 轉廣漢太守。

translations.literal: Transferred Administrator of Guanghan.
translations.idiomatic: He transferred to Guanghan prefect.

sentences.zh: 郡多滯訟，有經三十年而不決者，處詳其枉直，一朝決遣。

translations.literal: The commandery had many stagnant lawsuits; there were those passing thirty years yet undecided; Chu examined their crooked and straight; one morning decided and dispatched them.
translations.idiomatic: He cleared a backlog of lawsuits some thirty years old in a single day.

sentences.zh: 以母老罷歸。

translations.literal: Because mother was old he dismissed office and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned to care for his aging mother.

sentences.zh: 尋除楚內史，未之官，徵拜散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Soon removed as Chu interior steward; before reaching office summoned Cavalier Attendant in Regular Service.
translations.idiomatic: Named Chu interior steward before arrival he was recalled as imperial attendant.

sentences.zh: 處曰：「古人辭大不辭小。

translations.literal: Chu said: "The ancients declined great posts but not small ones."
translations.idiomatic: He cited the maxim that gentlemen refuse grand titles but not humble duties.

sentences.zh: 」乃先之楚。

translations.literal: " Thereupon first went to Chu.
translations.idiomatic: He insisted on taking the Chu post first.

sentences.zh: 而郡既經喪亂，新舊雜居，風俗未一，處敦以教義，又檢屍骸無主及白骨在野收葬之，然始就-{征}-，遠近稱歎。

translations.literal: Yet the commandery had already passed mourning and chaos; old and new dwelt mixed; customs were not uniform; Chu earnestly applied teaching and principle; again inspected corpses without masters and white bones in the wilds and gathered and buried them; only then proceeded to summons—far and near praised and sighed.
translations.idiomatic: Amid war-ravaged Chu he taught moral order, buried abandoned dead, then answered the capital summons to universal praise.

sentences.zh: 及居近侍，多所規諷。

translations.literal: When dwelling near attendant service he much remonstrated and admonished by implication.
translations.idiomatic: As palace attendant he repeatedly offered blunt counsel.

sentences.zh: 遷御史中丞，凡所糾劾，不避寵戚。

translations.literal: Promoted Palace Assistant Imperial Clerk; whatever he impeached did not avoid favored kin.
translations.idiomatic: As imperial censor he impeached even imperial favorites.

sentences.zh: 梁王肜違法，處深文案之。

translations.literal: Prince Liang Xiong violated law; Chu deeply documented him in legal documents.
translations.idiomatic: He built a legal case against Prince Sima Xiong of Liang.

sentences.zh: 及氐人齊萬年反，朝臣惡處強直，皆曰：「處，呉之名將子也，忠烈果毅。

translations.literal: When Di man Qi Wannian rebelled, court ministers hated Chu's strength and uprightness—all said: "Chu is Wu's famous general's son; loyal, fierce, resolute, daring."
translations.idiomatic: When Qi Wannian rose, ministers jealous of Zhou Chu praised his martial pedigree to send him west.

sentences.zh: 」乃使隸夏侯駿西-{征}-。

translations.literal: " Thereupon made him subordinate to Xia Houjun's western expedition.
translations.idiomatic: They assigned him under Xia Houjun's western campaign.

sentences.zh: 伏波將軍孫秀知其將死，謂之曰：「卿有老母，可以此辭也。

translations.literal: General Who Calms Waves Sun Xiu knew he would die; said to him: "You have an old mother—you may use this to decline."
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xiu warned him to plead his mother's age and refuse.

sentences.zh: 」處曰：「忠孝之道，安得兩全！

translations.literal: " Chu said: "The way of loyalty and filial piety—how can both be complete!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Chu replied that loyalty and filial duty rarely coincide.

sentences.zh: 既辭親事君，父母復安得而子乎？

translations.literal: " Having declined kin to serve lord—how can parents again treat one as son?"
translations.idiomatic: Having chosen service over family, he could hardly cling to both.

sentences.zh: 今日是我死所也。

translations.literal: " Today is my place of death."
translations.idiomatic: "This field is where I die."

sentences.zh: 」萬年聞之，曰：「周府君昔臨新平，我知其爲人，才兼文武，若專斷而來，不可當也。

translations.literal: " Wannian hearing it said: "Prefect Zhou formerly administered Xinping—I know his conduct—talent spans civil and military—if he comes with sole discretion he cannot be resisted."
translations.idiomatic: Qi Wannian respected Zhou Chu's Xinping record and feared him if free to command.

sentences.zh: 如受制於人，此成擒耳。

translations.literal: " If controlled by others—this becomes capture."
translations.idiomatic: Controlled by jealous generals, Zhou Chu would fall easily.

sentences.zh: 」既而梁王肜爲-{征}-西大將軍、都督關中諸軍事。

translations.literal: " Soon Prince Liang Xiong became General Who Conquers the West and supervised Guanzhong military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Xiong soon took western command over Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 處知肜不平，必當陷己，自以人臣盡節，不宜辭憚，乃悲慨即路，志不生還。

translations.literal: Chu knew Xiong was unfair—surely would trap him—himself thinking as minister fulfilling integrity ought not decline fear—thereupon sorrowfully took the road—intent not to live returning.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing Sima Xiong would sacrifice him, Zhou Chu marched anyway, expecting no return.

sentences.zh: 中書令陳准知肜將逞宿憾，乃言於朝曰：「駿及梁王皆是貴戚，非將率之才，進不求名，退不畏咎。

translations.literal: Palace Secretariat Director Chen Zhun knew Xiong would indulge old resentment—thereupon spoke in court saying: "Jun and Prince Liang both are noble kin—not talent of general leadership—advance not seeking fame; retreat not fearing blame."
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhun warned that Xia Houjun and Sima Xiong were courtiers, not generals.

sentences.zh: 周處呉人，忠勇果勁，有怨無援，將必喪身。

translations.literal: Zhou Chu a Wu man—loyal, brave, stalwart—bearing grudges without aid—surely will lose body."
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Chu, a Wu outsider without allies, would die uselessly.

sentences.zh: 宜詔孟觀以精兵萬人，爲處前鋒，必能殄寇。

translations.literal: " It is fitting to edict Meng Guan with elite troops ten thousand men as Chu's van—surely able to exterminate the bandits."
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhun urged sending Meng Guan with ten thousand veterans ahead of Zhou Chu.

sentences.zh: 不然，肜當使處先驅，其敗必也。

translations.literal: " Otherwise Xiong will make Chu vanguard—the defeat is certain."
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise Sima Xiong would waste Zhou Chu as a forlorn hope.

sentences.zh: 」朝廷不從。

translations.literal: " The court did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: The court ignored him.

sentences.zh: 時賊屯梁山，有眾七萬，而駿逼處以五千兵擊之。

translations.literal: At the time bandits encamped at Liang Mountain—had multitude seventy thousand—yet Jun pressed Chu with five thousand troops to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Wannian held Liang Mountain with seventy thousand men while Xia Houjun ordered Zhou Chu forward with only five thousand.

sentences.zh: 處曰：「軍無-{後}-繼，必至覆敗，雖在亡身，爲國取恥。

translations.literal: Chu said: "The army lacks rear support—surely will arrive at overturned defeat—although body perishes—it takes shame for the state."
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Chu warned that unsupported troops would collapse and shame Jin.

sentences.zh: 」肜復命處進討，乃與振威將軍盧播、雍州刺史解系攻萬年於六陌。

translations.literal: " Xiong again ordered Chu advance and strike—thereupon together with General Who Displays Might Lu Bo and Yong Province Inspector Xie Xi attacked Wannian at Liumo.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Xiong insisted; Zhou Chu joined Lu Bo and Xie Xi against Qi Wannian at Liumo.

sentences.zh: 將戰，處軍人未食，肜促令速進，而絶其-{後}-繼。

translations.literal: About to battle—Chu's soldiers had not eaten—Xiong urged order quick advance—and cut off his rear support.
translations.idiomatic: Before battle Sima Xiong denied Zhou Chu food and reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 處知必敗，賦詩曰：「去去世事已，策馬觀西戎。

translations.literal: Chu knew he must fail—composed poem saying: "Gone gone—world affairs ended—whip horse viewing western Rong."
translations.idiomatic: Foreseeing doom Zhou Chu composed verse on riding west to face the tribes.

sentences.zh: 藜藿甘粱黍，期之克令終。

translations.literal: " Pigweed sweet—millet fine—I hope for this to achieve good end."
translations.idiomatic: He prayed humble fare might lead to an honorable death.

sentences.zh: 」言畢而戰，自旦及暮，斬首萬計。

translations.literal: " Words finished then battled—from dawn to dusk—beheaded ten thousand by estimate.
translations.idiomatic: He fought from dawn to dusk, claiming myriad heads.

sentences.zh: 弦絶矢盡，播、系不救。

translations.literal: Bowstrings snapped arrows exhausted—Lu Bo, Xie Xi did not rescue.
translations.idiomatic: His arrows ran out while Lu Bo and Xie Xi withheld aid.

sentences.zh: 左右勸退，處按劍曰：「此是吾效節授命之日，何退之爲！

translations.literal: Left and right urged retreat—Chu grasped sword saying: "This is my day to display integrity and give life—what retreat is there!"
translations.idiomatic: His officers urged retreat; he drew his sword and refused.

sentences.zh: 且古者良將受命，鑿凶門以出，蓋有進無退也。

translations.literal: " Moreover ancient fine generals receiving orders carved ill omen gate to exit—covering advance without retreat."
translations.idiomatic: He cited generals who marched through the funeral gate—never turning back.

sentences.zh: 今諸軍負信，勢必不振。

translations.literal: " Now the various armies betray faith—momentum surely cannot surge."
translations.idiomatic: Now allies had broken faith—morale was broken.

sentences.zh: 我爲大臣，以身徇國，不亦可乎！

translations.literal: " I am great minister—using body following state—is it not allowed!"
translations.idiomatic: As a senior minister he would die for the realm.

sentences.zh: 」遂力戰而沒。

translations.literal: " Thereupon fought with strength and perished.
translations.idiomatic: He fought until he fell.

sentences.zh: 追贈平西將軍，賜錢百萬，葬地一頃，京城地五十畝爲第，又賜王家近田五頃。

translations.literal: Posthumously awarded General Who Pacifies the West; granted cash one million; burial land one qing; capital city land fifty mu for mansion; again granted Wang family near fields five qing.
translations.idiomatic: The court posthumously named him General Who Pacifies the West with cash, burial plots, and farmland.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「處母年老，加以遠人，朕毎湣念，給其醫藥酒米，賜以終年。」

translations.literal: Edict said: "Chu's mother is old and moreover distant person—We always pity and remember—supply her medicine, ale, and rice—grant for whole year."
translations.idiomatic: An edict pensioned his elderly mother with grain and medicine.

sentences.zh: 處著《默語》三十篇及《風土記》，並撰集《呉書》。

translations.literal: Chu authored thirty chapters Silent Words and Record of Local Customs—also compiled compiled Wu Record.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Silent Words, the Record of Local Customs, and helped compile the Wu history.

sentences.zh: 時潘-{岳}-奉詔作《關中詩》曰：「周徇師令，身膏齊斧。

translations.literal: At the time Pan Yue by edict composed Guanzhong Poem saying: "Zhou obeyed army command—body greased Qi axe."
translations.idiomatic: Pan Yue's mandated poem praised Zhou Chu's martyrdom.

sentences.zh: 人之-{雲}-亡，貞節克舉。

translations.literal: "Men said him gone—yet steadfast honor endured."
translations.idiomatic: It hailed his death as proof of steadfast virtue.

sentences.zh: 」又西戎校尉閻纘亦上詩-{云}-：「周全其節，令問不已。

translations.literal: " Also Colonel of Western Rong Yan Zuan also submitted poem stating: "Zhou fulfilled his integrity—fine fame unending."
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zuan likewise memorialized verse honoring Zhou Chu.

sentences.zh: 身雖-{云}-沒，書名良史。

translations.literal: "Though men declare him dead—his name will shine in history."
translations.idiomatic: Though dead, his name would grace the histories.

sentences.zh: 」及元帝爲晉王，將加處策諡，太常賀循議曰：「處履德清方，才量高出；

translations.literal: " When Prince Yuan was Prince of Jin—about to add Chu's posthumous verdict—Grand Master of Ceremonies He Xun deliberated saying: "Chu tread virtue pure and upright—talent and measure high surpassing."
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Rui prepared Zhou Chu's posthumous title, He Xun praised his purity and talent.

sentences.zh: 曆守四郡，安人立政；

translations.literal: " Successively guarded four commanderies—pacified people established governance."
translations.idiomatic: He had governed four prefectures with kindness.

sentences.zh: 入司百僚，貞節不撓；

translations.literal: " Entered supervising hundred officials—chaste integrity unyielding."
translations.idiomatic: At court he kept principled counsel.

sentences.zh: 在戎致身，見危授命：此皆忠賢之茂實，烈士之遠節。

translations.literal: " In army brought body—seeing peril entrusted life—these all are loyal worthy thick fruits—martyr knight far integrity."
translations.idiomatic: He died in arms facing peril—the essence of martyr loyalty.

sentences.zh: 案諡法執德不回曰孝。

translations.literal: " Checking posthumous law—holding virtue not turning is called Xiao."
translations.idiomatic: By canon law steadfast virtue merits the epithet Xiao.

sentences.zh: 」遂以諡焉。

translations.literal: " Thereupon applied posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: They granted him the epithet Xiao.

sentences.zh: 有三子：玘、靖、劄。

translations.literal: He had three sons: Qi, Jing, Zha.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Zhou Qi, Zhou Jing, and Zhou Zha.

sentences.zh: 靖早卒，玘、劄並知名。

translations.literal: Jing died early; Qi and Zha both had reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Jing died young; Qi and Zha became noted.

translations.literal: Equals sign, table continuation marker.
translations.idiomatic: Section divider in tabular layout.

sentences.zh: 玘

translations.literal: Qi — name label.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Qi.

translations.literal: Equals sign, table continuation marker.
translations.idiomatic: Section divider in tabular layout.

sentences.zh: 玘字宣佩。

translations.literal: Qi's courtesy name was Xuanpei.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Qi, courtesy Xuanpei.

sentences.zh: 強毅沈斷有父風，而文學不及。

translations.literal: Strong, resolute, deep, decisive—had father's manner—but literary learning did not reach.
translations.idiomatic: He matched his father's toughness though less scholarly.

sentences.zh: 閉門潔己，不妄交遊，士友咸望風敬憚焉，故名重一方。

translations.literal: Closed gate purified self—did not rashly associate and roam—gentlemen and friends all by wind admired and feared him—therefore fame weighed one region.
translations.idiomatic: Reclusive and austere, he impressed contemporaries with stern dignity.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，州郡命，不就。

translations.literal: At weak capping age province and commandery ordered him—he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He refused office until adulthood.

sentences.zh: 刺史初到，召爲別駕從事，虛己備禮，方始應命。

translations.literal: When Inspector first arrived summoned him as Assistant Administrator Clerk—emptying self prepared ritual—only then responded to order.
translations.idiomatic: Only when a new inspector humbled himself with full ceremony did Zhou Qi agree to serve as aide.

sentences.zh: 累薦名宰府，舉秀才，除議郎。

translations.literal: Repeatedly recommended to eminent ministerial offices—raised Worthy Youth—removed Gentleman Consultant.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended to high office, he rose Worthy and became Consultant Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 太安初，妖賊張昌、丘沈等聚眾-{於}-江夏，百姓從之如歸。

translations.literal: Early in Taian, demon bandits Zhang Chang, Qiu Shen and others gathered masses at Jiangxia—commoners followed them like returning home.
translations.idiomatic: In Taian's turmoil Zhang Chang and Qiu Shen rallied Jiangxia until people flocked to them.

sentences.zh: 惠帝使監軍華宏討之，敗於障山。

translations.literal: Emperor Hui sent inspector-at-war Hua Hong to strike them—defeated at Zhang Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Hui sent Hua Hong, who lost at Zhangshan.

sentences.zh: 昌等浸盛，殺平南將軍羊伊，鎮南大將軍、新野王歆等，所在覆沒。

translations.literal: Chang and others gradually flourished—killed General Who Pacifies the South Yang Yi—General Who Guards the South, Prince Xinyang Xin and others—wherever located overturned and drowned.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chang killed Yang Yi and Prince Sima Xin until garrisons collapsed everywhere.

sentences.zh: 昌別率封-{雲}-攻徐州，石冰攻揚州，刺史陳徽出奔，冰遂略有揚土。

translations.literal: Chang separately led Feng Yun assault Xu Province—Shi Bing assaulted Yang Province—Inspector Chen Hui fled out—Bing thereupon seized Yang lands in outline.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chang's lieutenants Feng Yun and Shi Bing swept Xu and Yang until Chen Hui fled.

sentences.zh: 玘密欲討冰，潛結前南平內史王矩，共推呉興太守顧秘都督揚州九郡軍事，及江東人士同起義兵，斬冰所置呉興太守區山及諸長史。

translations.literal: Qi secretly wished to strike Bing—secretly allied former Nanping interior steward Wang Ju—together promoted Wu Xing Administrator Gu Mi supervisor of Yang Province nine commanderies military affairs—and Jiangdong gentlemen together raised righteous troops—executed Bing's appointed Wu Xing Administrator Ou Shan and various senior clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Qi allied Wang Ju and Gu Mi to raise Jiangdong forces, killing Shi Bing's officers.

sentences.zh: 冰遣其將羌毒領數萬人距玘，玘臨陣斬毒。

translations.literal: Bing dispatched his general Qiang Du leading tens of thousands to oppose Qi—Qi at battle array executed Du.
translations.idiomatic: He slew Shi Bing's general Qiang Du in battle.

sentences.zh: 時右將軍陳敏自廣陵率眾助圮，斬冰別率趙驡於蕪湖，因與玘俱前攻冰-{於}-建康。

translations.literal: At the time Right General Chen Min from Guangling led masses aiding Qi—executed Bing's separate leader Zhao Ji at Wuhu—thereupon together with Qi both advanced attacking Bing at Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Min joined Zhou Qi, defeated Zhao Ji at Wuhu, and marched on Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 冰北走投封-{雲}-，-{雲}-司馬張統斬-{雲}-、冰以降，徐、揚並平。

translations.literal: Bing fled north seeking Feng Yun—Yun's Major Zhang Tong executed Yun and Bing to surrender—Xu and Yang together pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Bing fled to Feng Yun; Zhang Tong slew both bandit leaders and restored Xu and Yang.

sentences.zh: 玘不言功賞，散眾還家。

translations.literal: Qi did not speak of merit rewards—dispersed hosts returning home.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Qi disbanded his volunteers without seeking rewards.

sentences.zh: 陳敏反於揚州，以圮爲安豐太守，加四品將軍。

translations.literal: Chen Min rebelled at Yang Province—appointed Qi Administrator of Anfeng—added fourth-rank general.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Min rebelled he named Zhou Qi prefect of Anfeng.

sentences.zh: 玘稱疾不行，密遣使告鎮東將軍劉准，令發兵臨江，己爲內應，翦發爲信。

translations.literal: Qi claimed illness did not proceed—secretly dispatched envoy informing General Who Guards the East Liu Zhun ordering raise troops approaching river—himself as inner response—cut hair as pledge.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Qi feigned illness while urging Liu Zhun to march east, cutting his hair as covenant.

sentences.zh: 准在壽春，遣督護衡彥率眾而東。

translations.literal: Zhun was at Shouchun—dispatched Protector Heng Yan leading masses eastward.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhun at Shouchun sent Heng Yan eastward.

sentences.zh: 時敏弟昶爲廣武將軍、曆陽內史，以呉興錢廣爲司馬。

translations.literal: At the time Min's younger brother Chang was General Who Displays Martial Might and Liyang interior steward—with Wu Xing Qian Guang as Major.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Min's brother Chen Chang held Liyang with Qian Guang as major.

sentences.zh: 玘密諷廣殺昶。

translations.literal: Qi secretly exhorted Guang kill Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Qi persuaded Qian Guang to assassinate Chen Chang.

sentences.zh: 玘與顧榮、甘卓等以兵攻敏，敏眾奔潰，單馬北走，獲之-{於}-江乘界，斬之-{於}-建康，夷三族。

translations.literal: Qi together with Gu Rong, Gan Zhuo and others with troops attacked Min—Min's multitude fled in collapse—single horse fled north—captured him at Jiangcheng boundary—executed him at Jiankang—extinguished three clans.
translations.idiomatic: With Gu Rong and Gan Zhuo he shattered Chen Min, captured him at Jiangcheng, and executed him at Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 東海王越聞其名，召爲參軍。

translations.literal: Prince Donghai Sima Yue heard his name and summoned him as staff adviser.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yue enlisted Zhou Qi as military adviser.

sentences.zh: 詔補尚書郎、散騎郎，並不行。

translations.literal: Edict supplemented Palace Secretariat Gentleman and Cavalier Gentleman—both he did not proceed.
translations.idiomatic: He declined concurrent posts as secretary and cavalry gentleman.

sentences.zh: 元帝初鎮江左，以玘爲倉曹屬。

translations.literal: When Prince Yuan first held Jiangzuo he appointed Qi as Granary Bureau aide.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yuan Sima Rui named him aide in the granary bureau.

sentences.zh: 初，呉興人錢璯亦起義兵討陳敏，越命爲建武將軍，使率其屬會於京都。

translations.literal: Earlier Wu Xing man Qian Hao also raised righteous troops attacking Chen Min—Yue appointed him General Who Establishes Might—ordered him lead his followers rally at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Hao of Wu Xing had joined the loyalists; Sima Yue commissioned him to march on the capital.

sentences.zh: 璯至廣陵，聞劉聰逼洛陽，畏懦不敢進。

translations.literal: Hao reached Guangling—heard Liu Cong pressing Luoyang—cowardly feared advancing.
translations.idiomatic: At Guangling Qian Hao learned Liu Cong threatened Luoyang and stalled in fear.

sentences.zh: 帝促以軍期，璯乃謀反。

translations.literal: The Emperor urged military deadline—Hao thereupon plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Rui pressed his deadline, Qian Hao rebelled.

sentences.zh: 時王敦遷尚書，當應徵與璯俱西。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Dun was promoted Palace Secretariat Director—should respond summons going west with Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun was ordered west alongside Qian Hao.

sentences.zh: 璯陰欲殺敦，藉以舉事，敦聞之，奔告帝。

translations.literal: Hao secretly wished to kill Dun—borrow pretext to raise affair—Dun hearing it fled and reported the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Hao planned to murder Wang Dun and seize power; Wang Dun fled to warn the throne.

sentences.zh: 璯遂殺度支校尉陳豐，焚燒邸閣，自號平西大將軍、八州都督，劫孫皓子充，立爲呉王，既而殺之。

translations.literal: Hao thereupon killed Supplies Colonel Chen Feng—burned granaries—self-proclaimed General Who Pacifies the West and supervisor of eight provinces—kidnapped Sun Hao's son Chong—installed him Wu king—afterward killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Hao killed Chen Feng, torched depots, crowned himself western commander, briefly enthroned Sun Chong as Wu king, then slew him.

sentences.zh: 來寇圮縣。

translations.literal: He came raiding Qi county.
translations.idiomatic: He marched against Zhou Qi's home county.

sentences.zh: 帝遣將軍郭逸、郡尉宋典等討之，並以兵少未敢前。

translations.literal: The Emperor dispatched General Guo Yi, county commandant Song Dian and others to strike them—all because troops few did not dare advance.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial generals hesitated for lack of numbers.

sentences.zh: 玘復率合鄕里義眾，與逸等俱進，討璯，斬之，傳首-{於}-建康。

translations.literal: Qi again led combined village righteous hosts together with Yi and others advancing—struck Hao—executed him—sent head to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Qi rallied militia, joined Guo Yi, beheaded Qian Hao, and sent his head to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 玘三定江南，開復王略，帝嘉其勳，以玘行建威將軍、呉興太守，封烏程縣侯。

translations.literal: Qi thrice pacified Jiangnan—opened and restored royal strategy—the Emperor praised his merit—appointed Qi acting General Who Establishes Might and Wu Xing Administrator—enfeoffed Baron of Wucheng county.
translations.idiomatic: For thrice saving the south Sima Rui made him General Who Establishes Might, prefect of Wu Xing, and Baron of Wucheng.

sentences.zh: 呉興寇亂之-{後}-，百姓饑饉，盜賊公行，玘甚有威惠，百姓敬愛之，期年之間，境內寧謐。

translations.literal: After Wu Xing bandit chaos common people starved—bandits traveled openly—Qi had great awe-inspiring kindness—common people revered and loved him—within one year boundary interior peaceful still.
translations.idiomatic: He restored order and famine relief until Wu Xing knew peace within a year.

sentences.zh: 帝以圮頻興義兵，勳誠並茂，乃以陽羨及長城之西鄕、丹陽之永世別爲義興郡，以彰其功焉。

translations.literal: The Emperor because Qi frequently raised righteous troops—merit and loyalty both luxuriant—thereupon made Yangxian and western townships of Changcheng and Yongshi of Danyang separately Yixing commandery—to manifest his merit.
translations.idiomatic: To honor him Sima Rui carved Yixing commandery from Yangxian, Changcheng, and Danyang lands.

sentences.zh: 玘宗族強盛，人情所歸，帝疑憚之。

translations.literal: Qi's lineage clan was strong and flourishing—human hearts attached—the Emperor suspected and dreaded him.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou clan's power unsettled Sima Rui.

sentences.zh: -{於}-時中州人士佐佑王業，而圮自以爲不得調，內懷怨望，復爲刁協輕之，恥恚愈甚。

translations.literal: At that time central plain gentlemen aided king's enterprise—yet Qi himself thought he received no proper appointments—inward bore resentment—again was slighted by Diao Xie—shame and rage grew extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Northerners dominated court while Zhou Qi felt slighted by low appointments and Diao Xie's contempt.

sentences.zh: 時鎮東將軍祭酒東萊王恢亦爲周凱所侮，乃與圮陰謀誅諸執政，推玘及戴若思與諸南士共奉帝以經緯世事。

translations.literal: At the time General Who Guards the East libationer Wang Hui of Donglai was also insulted by Zhou Kai—thereupon with Qi secretly plotted executing various administrators—promoting Qi and Dai Ruosi with southern gentlemen jointly supporting the Emperor to order worldly affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hui, insulted by Zhou Kai, conspired with Zhou Qi and Dai Ruosi to purge northern ministers.

sentences.zh: 先是，流人帥夏鐵等寓於淮、泗，恢陰書與鐵，令起兵，己當與玘以三呉應之。

translations.literal: Earlier refugee chief Xia Tie and others sojourned at Huai and Si—Hui secretly wrote Tie ordering raise troops—himself would with Qi using San Wu respond.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hui urged refugee leader Xia Tie to rise on the Huai while he and Zhou Qi would answer from Wu.

sentences.zh: 建興初，鐵已聚眾數百人，臨淮太守蔡豹斬鐵以聞。

translations.literal: Early Jianxing Tie had already gathered several hundred masses—Linhuai Administrator Cai Bao executed Tie and reported.
translations.idiomatic: Before the plot matured Cai Bao killed Xia Tie.

sentences.zh: 恢聞鐵死，懼罪，奔於玘，玘殺之，埋於豕牢。

translations.literal: Hui hearing Tie died feared crime—fled to Qi—Qi killed him—buried him in pig sty.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hui fled to Zhou Qi, who executed him and dumped the body in a pigpen.

sentences.zh: 帝聞而秘之，召玘爲鎮東司馬，未到，復改授建武將軍、南郡太守。

translations.literal: The Emperor hearing kept it secret—summoned Qi as General Who Guards the East Major—before arriving again changed investiture General Who Establishes Might and Nan Commandery Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Rui hushed the scandal but transferred Zhou Qi through successive posts to sideline him.

sentences.zh: 圮既南行，至蕪湖，又下令曰：「玘奕世忠烈，義誠顯著，孤所欽喜。

translations.literal: After Qi went south reaching Wuhu—again issued order saying: "Qi generations loyal and fierce—righteous sincerity manifest—Our lone person admires and rejoices."
translations.idiomatic: At Wuhu Sima Rui issued an edict praising the Zhou family's loyalty.

sentences.zh: 今以爲軍諮祭酒，將軍如故，進爵爲公，祿秩僚屬一同開國之例。

translations.literal: " Now appoint Army Counsel Libationer—general as before—advance noble rank to duke—salary ranks and staff followers same as founding state's precedent."
translations.idiomatic: He named Zhou Qi army counselor while promoting him to duke with princely stipends.

sentences.zh: 」玘忿-{於}-回易，又知其謀泄，遂憂憤發背而卒，時年五十六。

translations.literal: " Qi resented the reversal—also knew his plot leaked—thereupon worried and indignant developed back abscess and died—at the time age fifty-six.
translations.idiomatic: Bitter at the empty honor and exposed plot, Zhou Qi died of an infected carbuncle at fifty-six.

sentences.zh: 將卒，謂之勰曰：「殺我者諸傖子，能復之，乃吾子也。

translations.literal: About to die said to Xie: "Those who kill me are the various rustic fellows—he who can avenge them is my son."
translations.idiomatic: He told his son Zhou Xie that northern courtiers had killed him and must be avenged.

sentences.zh: 」呉人謂中州人曰「傖」，故-{云}-耳。

translations.literal: " Wu men called central plain men 'rustics'—therefore stated thus."
translations.idiomatic: Wu people sneered at northerners as 'rustics'—hence his dying words.

sentences.zh: 贈輔國將軍，諡曰忠烈。

translations.literal: Posthumously awarded General Who Supports the State—posthumous title Zhonglie.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously named General Who Supports the State with epithet Zhonglie.

sentences.zh: 子勰嗣。

translations.literal: Son Xie succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhou Xie inherited the title.

translations.literal: Double equals sign table continuation marker.
translations.idiomatic: Section divider in tabular layout.

sentences.zh: 勰

translations.literal: Xie — name label.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Xie.

sentences.zh: 勰字彥和。

translations.literal: Xie's courtesy name was Yanhe.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Xie, courtesy Yanhe.

sentences.zh: 常緘父言。

translations.literal: Often sealed father's words.
translations.idiomatic: He nursed his father's grudge against northern ministers.

sentences.zh: 時中國亡官失守之士避亂來者，多居顯位，駕御呉人，呉人頗怨。

translations.literal: At the time central plain lost-office defeated-garrison gentlemen fleeing turmoil came—many occupied eminent positions—riding and controlling Wu men—Wu men quite resented.
translations.idiomatic: Refugee officials held power over Wu families, stirring deep resentment.

sentences.zh: 勰因之欲起兵，潛結呉興郡功曹徐馥。

translations.literal: Xie because of this wished to raise troops—secretly allied Wu Xing merit clerk Xu Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Xie plotted rebellion with Xu Fu of Wu Xing.

sentences.zh: 馥家有部曲，勰使馥矯稱叔父劄命以合眾，豪俠樂亂者翕然附之，以討王導、刁協爲名。

translations.literal: Fu's household had personal troops—Xie made Fu falsely proclaim uncle Zha's order to assemble masses—bold braves delighting in chaos attached like wind—using strike Wang Dao and Diao Xie as name.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Fu forged orders from Zhou Zha to raise troops against Wang Dao and Diao Xie.

sentences.zh: 孫皓族人弼亦起兵於廣德以應之。

translations.literal: Sun Hao clansman Bi also raised troops at Guangde to respond.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Bi of Sun Hao's clan rose at Guangde in support.

sentences.zh: 馥殺呉興太守袁琇，有眾數千，將奉劄爲主。

translations.literal: Fu killed Wu Xing Administrator Yuan Xiu—had hosts several thousand—was about to install Zha as lord.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Fu killed Prefect Yuan Xiu and meant to enthrone Zhou Zha.

sentences.zh: 時劄以疾歸家，聞而大驚，乃告亂-{於}-義興太守孔侃。

translations.literal: At the time Zha because illness returned home—hearing greatly startled—thereupon reported chaos to Yixing Administrator Kong Kan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Zha, home ill, denounced the plot to Kong Kan.

sentences.zh: 勰知劄不同，不敢發兵。

translations.literal: Xie knew Zha did not agree—did not dare dispatch troops.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Xie held back when Zhou Zha refused.

sentences.zh: 馥黨懼，攻馥，殺之。

translations.literal: Fu's party feared—attacked Fu—killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Fu's followers panicked and killed him.

sentences.zh: 孫弼眾亦潰，宣城太守陶猷滅之。

translations.literal: Sun Bi's multitude also collapsed—Xuancheng Administrator Tao You extinguished them.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Bi scattered; Tao You of Xuancheng destroyed his band.

sentences.zh: 元帝以周氏奕世豪望，呉人所宗，故不窮治，撫之如舊。

translations.literal: Prince Yuan because Zhou house generations eminent expectation—Wu people's object—therefore did not exhaust prosecution—soothed them as of old.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Rui avoided punishing the Zhou clan to keep Wu loyal.

sentences.zh: 勰爲劄所責，失志歸家，淫侈縱恣，毎謂人曰：「人生幾時，但當快意耳。

translations.literal: Xie was blamed by Zha—lost ambition returned home—debauchery and extravagance unleashed—often said to people: "Human life how many moments—only ought seek pleasure."
translations.idiomatic: Rebuked by Zhou Zha, Zhou Xie sank into dissipation.

sentences.zh: 」終於臨淮太守。

translations.literal: " Ended as Linhuai Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: He died serving as Linhuai prefect.

sentences.zh: 彝

translations.literal: Yi — name label.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yi.

sentences.zh: 勰弟彝，少知名，元帝辟爲丞相掾，早亡。

translations.literal: Xie's younger brother Yi—little known reputation—Prince Yuan summoned as Chancellor aide—died early.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yi, Zhou Xie's brother, died young after joining Sima Rui's staff.

translations.literal: Equals marker Zhou Zha equals table row.
translations.idiomatic: Table marker introducing Zhou Zha.

sentences.zh: 劄字宣季。

translations.literal: Zha's courtesy name was Xuanji.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Zha, courtesy Xuanji.

sentences.zh: 性矜險好利，外方內荏，少以豪右自處，州郡辟命皆不就。

translations.literal: Nature arrogant perilous fond of profit—outward square inward weak—young considered himself magnate—province and commandery summons all did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Arrogant, grasping, and outwardly bold yet timid, he spurned office until middle age.

sentences.zh: 察孝廉，除郎中、大司馬齊王冏參軍。

translations.literal: Recommended Filially Incorrupt—removed Gentleman of the Palace—Grand Marshal Prince Qi Sima Jiong staff adviser.
translations.idiomatic: He rose Worthy, served Sima Jiong, and entered the palace corps.

sentences.zh: 出補句容令，遷呉國上軍將軍。

translations.literal: Sent out supplemented Gouling magistrate—promoted Wu kingdom Upper Army general.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Gouling and became Wu kingdom general.

sentences.zh: 辟東海王越參軍，不就。

translations.literal: Summoned Prince Donghai Yue staff adviser—did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He refused Sima Yue's invitation.

sentences.zh: 以討錢璯功，賜爵漳浦亭侯。

translations.literal: By merit striking Qian Hao granted noble rank Zhangpu precinct baron.
translations.idiomatic: He earned the Zhangpu barony for defeating Qian Hao.

sentences.zh: 元帝爲丞相，表劄爲甯遠將軍、曆陽內史，不之職，轉從事中郎。

translations.literal: Prince Yuan as Chancellor memorialized Zha as General Who Pacifies the Distance and Liyang interior steward—did not take office—transferred attendant clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Rui named him Liyang prefect but he became attendant clerk instead.

sentences.zh: 徐馥平，以劄爲奮武將軍、呉興內史，録前-{後}-功，改封東遷縣侯，進號-{征}-虜將軍、臨揚州江北軍事、東中郎將，鎮塗中，未之職，轉右將軍、都督石頭水陸軍事。

translations.literal: When Xu Fu was pacified—appointed Zha General Who Exerts Might and Wu Xing interior steward—recording former and later merit—changed enfeoffment Dongqian county baron—advanced title General Who Conquers the Caitiffs—supervising Jiangbei north of Yangzhou—East Central General—garrison Tuzhong—did not take office—transferred Right General—supervising Stone City land and water armies.
translations.idiomatic: After Xu Fu's defeat Zhou Zha stacked titles as Wu Xing prefect, Stone City commander, and general with shifting commissions.

sentences.zh: 劄腳疾，不堪拜，固讓經年，有司彈奏，不得已乃視職。

translations.literal: Zha foot ailment—could not bow—firmly declined full year—relevant office impeached—unavoidably then assumed duties.
translations.idiomatic: Lame and reluctant, he took office only under impeachment.

sentences.zh: 加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Added Cavalier Attendant in Regular Service.
translations.idiomatic: He received concurrent imperial attendant rank.

sentences.zh: 王敦舉兵攻石頭，劄開門應敦，故王師敗績。

translations.literal: Wang Dun raised troops attacking Stone City—Zha opened gates answering Dun—therefore royal army suffered defeat.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Dun struck Jiankang Zhou Zha opened Stone City to him.

sentences.zh: 敦轉劄爲光祿勳，尋補尚書。

translations.literal: Dun transferred Zha as Imperial Household Grandee—soon supplemented Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun moved him to household grandee then secretary.

sentences.zh: 頃之，遷右將軍、會稽內史。

translations.literal: Shortly promoted Right General and Kuaiji interior steward.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became Right General and Kuaiji prefect.

sentences.zh: 時劄兄靖子懋晉陵太守、清流亭侯，懋弟筵-{征}-虜將軍，呉興內史，筵弟贊大將軍從事中郎、武康縣侯，贊弟縉太子文學、都鄕侯，次兄子勰臨淮太守、烏程公。

translations.literal: At the time Zha's elder brother Jing's son Mao Jinling Administrator and Qingliu precinct baron—Mao's younger brother Yan General Who Conquers the Caitiffs and Wu Xing interior steward—Yan's younger brother Zan grand marshal aide and Wukang county baron—Zan's younger brother Jin heir literary attendant and Duxiang baron—next elder brother's son Xie Linhuai Administrator and Wucheng duke.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou clan held five noble posts across Jinling, Wu Xing, and the heir's court.

sentences.zh: 劄一門五侯，並居列位，呉士貴盛，莫與爲比，王敦深忌之。

translations.literal: Zha one gate five marquises—all occupied ranked positions—Wu gentry noble flourishing—none compared—with him—Wang Dun deeply envied them.
translations.idiomatic: Five Zhou nobles outshone every Wu family and drew Wang Dun's jealousy.

sentences.zh: -{後}-筵喪母，送者千數，敦益憚焉。

translations.literal: Later Yan mourned mother—senders numbered thousands—Dun grew more fearful.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Yan buried his mother thousands attended, alarming Wang Dun.

sentences.zh: 及敦疾，錢風以周氏宗強，與沈充權勢相侔，欲自托於充，謀滅周氏，使充得專威揚土，乃説敦曰：「夫有國者患於強逼，自古釁難恆必由之。

translations.literal: When Dun fell ill Qian Feng because Zhou clan lineage strong—with Shen Chong power matched—wished self attach to Chong—plot extinguish Zhou clan—letting Chong monopolize awe Yang lands—thereupon persuaded Dun saying: "Those possessing state worry strong coercion—from ancient times calamity and difficulty always arises thus."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun's lieutenant Qian Feng urged him to destroy the Zhou and Shen clans before they threatened the realm.

translations.idiomatic: He marched on drums and secured the Han basin.

translations.literal: Zeng and others fled defending Wudang.
translations.idiomatic: Du Zeng bottled up in Wudang.

translations.literal: " Thereupon beyond expectation—again struck defeated him—Zeng fled away.
translations.idiomatic: He surprised Du Zeng again and drove him fleeing.

translations.idiomatic: Su Wen captured Du Zeng and allies for Wang Dun.

translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun executed Fifth Yi anyway.

translations.literal: Advanced rank General Who Pacifies the South—Bearer of Staff—supervisor and inspector as before.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to General Who Pacifies the South with unchanged command.
